slides.title: Who we are
bullets: Computational biology and chemistry group based in Edinburgh, founded 2009
Part of Tarnovell Bioscience Group since 2014, alongside in vitro biology, DMPK, chemistry, analytical and formulation laboratories
Bioinformaticians, computational chemists and data scientists working from a shared, version-controlled analysis platform

bullets.text: Every engagement starts from the biological question and ends with a decision the project team can act on

bullets: Clients: biotechs without in-house informatics, mid-size pharma teams needing extra capacity, and academic drug discovery units
slides.notes: Keep this short. The point is that we are scientists first and that the lab firms in the group can test what we predict.

slides.title: Bioinfromatics for drug discovery
bullets: Turns large biological datasets into decisions at each stage of a programme

bullets.text: Target identification: rank disease-linked genes from transcriptomics, genetics and literature-curated pathways
Target validation support: check expression in the relevant tissues, cell types and patient subgroups to guide functional testing
Mechanism of action: read out pathway responses to compound treatment from RNA-seq and proteomics
Biomarker candidates: propose response signatures for the patients most likley to respond, e.g. by tumour subtype
Safety signals: flag off-target and tissue-expression liabilities before chemistry is committed

bullets: Every analysis is reproducible: data provenance, versioned pipelines and an acceptance check before results are released
Outcome: fewer, better-evidenced targets and earlier no-go decisions, so lab budget goes on the compounds that matter
slides.notes: Adapted for the oncology pitch on 24/04. Check with Tomasz before sending.
